narrative: 黄金分割比三分法更为隐秘。这种图式依然在追问谁拥有空间，但这个较大的区域不再是一块生硬的三分之二板块。
一条从角落穿过一张脸、再穿过一扇门、最后延伸进空旷天气之中的螺旋线，可以显得理所当然，却不会显露出网格的痕迹。当观众需要一眼看懂整个图式时，这就不是对的工具。
动作场面的空间调度、喜剧调度，以及大多数常规覆盖镜头都生活在更简单的轴线上。如果你无法指出一条眼睛真正会顺着行进的曲线，那你只是在用数学做装饰。
画家们采用这些比例，是因为画布是静止不动的。而在一个运动镜头中，这条螺旋线必须在摇镜、行走和焦点变化中依然存活下来。
先设计好静态构图，再看看这个运镜是否依然保留了这条曲线。
how: phi网格把线条放在大约38%和62%的位置，比三分法的辅助线更靠内。黄金螺旋是一条路径，而不是一枚图章：从一个安静的角落开始，向着那张脸或视线的目标物盘旋而去。
保持摄影机水平。中等焦段（40mm到65mm）能保留这些比例。
超广角会通过扭曲房间来伪造出一条螺旋线。提示词：Golden-ratio spiral composition around [Subject], the eye traveling a harmonic curve rather than a grid.
when: 用它拍摄一次画意十足的静态镜头：一间经过设计的房间里的肖像，或一片真正有小径、树木和人物盘旋在一起的风景。不要在一个各质量块根本不在那条曲线上的镜头上强行叠加螺旋线。
vs: 三分法（Rule of Thirds）是更粗糙的默认规则，线条落在三分之一处，设置起来更快。中心构图（Centered Composition）把主体固定在轴线上，完全忽略螺旋线。
引导线（Leading Lines）如果建筑本身提供了这样的走势，也可以描绘出同样的曲线，但引导线并不要求符合黄金比例。如果画面是一个靶心，你要的其实是正中取景（Central Framing）。
examples_film: 画意电影常常在不明说的情况下依循这些比例来组织画面；《巴里·林登》（Barry Lyndon）把人物和家具安置在安静而和谐的房间之中。
《生命之树》（The Tree of Life）让风景、光线和一个渺小的身体共享一条盘旋线，而不是一张网格；《燃烧女子的肖像》（Portrait of a Lady on Fire）把面孔和炉火处理成一条缓慢流转的注意力曲线。
这是语法，而不是可以照搬的辅助线叠加图。
mistakes: 最常见的误用是三分法构图，再想象性地在上面叠加一条螺旋图形。破绽是一张脸落在33%的线上，而提示词只写了“黄金分割”。
修正方法：把质量块向内移到62%的位置，或者用次要物体真正搭建出一条眼睛可以追随的路径。

faq.q: 电影中的黄金比例（Golden Ratio）是什么？
faq.a: 它是使用接近1.618的比例进行构图，可以是一套phi网格，也可以是一条穿过各质量块的螺旋路径。主体是偏移的，但不像三分法线条那样生硬。眼睛应当去“行走”，而不是停靠在某一格里。

faq.q: 黄金比例（Golden Ratio）与三分法（Rule of Thirds）有何区别？
faq.a: 三分法把画面在33%处分割。phi比例则更接近38%和62%处分割。三分法是监视器上的默认网格。黄金比例构图则是一种更精细的比例主张，有时表现为一条曲线。两者都胜过意外的居中，但都不是法则。

faq.q: 什么时候该用黄金比例（Golden Ratio）？
faq.a: 当一个静态镜头或缓慢的固定镜头中，各质量块之间存在一条真实路径，而你希望呈现出不像学生辅助线那样生硬的秩序感时使用它。避免用于快速的空间调度、笑点，或任何一条螺旋线会显得虚假的镜头。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写黄金比例（Golden Ratio）的提示词？
faq.a: 要求螺旋线或phi比例的布局，并说明这条路径。示例：Golden-ratio spiral composition around [Subject], the eye traveling a harmonic curve rather than a grid。说明螺旋的起点和落点。避免使用神秘化的数学措辞。

narrative: Phi is a more secret order than thirds. The diagram still asks who owns space, but the large field is not a blunt two-thirds slab.

A spiral from a corner through a face, then through a doorway, then into empty weather, can feel inevitable without announcing a grid. It is the wrong tool when the audience needs the diagram in one glance.
Action geography, comedy blocking, and most coverage live on simpler axes. If you cannot point to a curve the eye actually rides, you are decorating with math.
Painters used these proportions because canvases hold still. In a moving shot the spiral has to survive a pan, a walk, and a focus change.
Design the still first, then see if the move keeps the curve.
how: A phi grid places lines at about 38 percent and 62 percent, inward of a thirds overlay. A golden spiral is a path, not a stamp: start at a quiet corner and coil toward the face or the object of the look.
Keep the camera level. Moderate glass (40mm to 65mm) preserves the proportions.
Ultra-wide will fake a spiral by bending the room. Prompt: Golden-ratio spiral composition around [Subject], the eye traveling a harmonic curve rather than a grid.
when: Use it on a painterly hold: a portrait in a designed room, a landscape where a path, a tree, and a figure actually coil. Do not overlay a spiral on a shot whose masses do not sit on that curve.
vs: Rule of Thirds is the coarser default, lines at one-third, faster to set. Centered Composition plants the subject on the axis and ignores the spiral.
Leading Lines can trace the same curve if the architecture supplies it, but leading lines do not require phi. If the picture is a bullseye, you wanted Central Framing.
examples_film: Painterly cinema often organizes near these proportions without announcing them. Barry Lyndon holds figures and furniture in quiet harmonic rooms.
The Tree of Life lets landscape, light, and a small body share a coil rather than a grid. Portrait of a Lady on Fire stages faces and firelight as a slow curve of attention.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is thirds with a spiral graphic imagined on top. The tell is a face on a 33 percent line and a prompt that only says golden.
The fix is to move the mass inward toward 62 percent, or to build an actual path of secondary objects the eye can ride.

faq.q: What is golden ratio in film?
faq.a: It is composition that uses proportions near 1.618, as a phi grid or as a spiral path through the masses. The subject is offset, but not as bluntly as on a thirds line. The eye is meant to travel, not to park on a cell.

faq.q: Golden Ratio vs Rule of Thirds
faq.a: Thirds splits the frame at 33 percent. Phi splits nearer 38 and 62 percent. Thirds is a default grid on a monitor. Golden-ratio composition is a tighter proportional claim, sometimes a curve. Both beat accidental centering. Neither is a law.

faq.q: When should I use golden ratio?
faq.a: Use it when a still or a slow hold has a real path of masses, and you want order that does not look like a student overlay. Skip it for fast geography, jokes, and any shot where the spiral would be a lie.

faq.q: How do I prompt golden ratio for AI image or video?
faq.a: Ask for a spiral or phi placement and name the path. Example: Golden-ratio spiral composition around [Subject], the eye traveling a harmonic curve rather than a grid. State the start of the coil and the landing point. Avoid mystic math talk.
